q: The normal force F_N exerted by a banked road is parallel to the road. (2024)
e: The normal force exerted by a banked road is perpendicular to the surface of the road.

q: The centripetal force is the force acting towards the centre of curvature. (2026)
e: By definition, centripetal force always acts towards the centre of curvature.

q: When a skater forms a circle, he has to lean outwards. (2024)
e: When a skater forms a circle, he must lean inwards towards the centre of curvature.

q: Centripetal force is the force acting on an object in circular motion which is directed towards the axis of rotation or centre of curvature. (2024)
e: Centripetal force is always directed towards the axis of rotation or centre of curvature.

q: Centrifugal force in circular motion is a real force. (2024)
e: Centrifugal force is an apparent or fictitious force, not a real force.

q: A ball attached to a string and whirled around a vertical circle experiences a net downward force at the bottom of the arc. (2025)
e: At the bottom of the arc, the net force on the ball is directed upwards towards the centre of the circle.

q: When whirling a body attached to a string, the tension force behaves as a centripetal force. (assume as whirling in horizontal circle) (2025)
e: The tension in the string acts toward the centre, serving as the required centripetal force.

q: A centripetal force makes the object to turn a curved path. (2025)
e: Centripetal force changes the direction of motion, forcing the object along a curved path.

q: Banking of roads involves lowering the outer edge of the curved road relative to the inner edge. (2025)
e: Banking of roads involves raising the outer edge of the curved road relative to the inner edge.

q: When a skater forms a circle, she has to lean outwards. (2025)
e: When a skater forms a circle, she must lean inwards towards the centre.

q: In the present of centripetal force, the object would move along a circle. (2025)
e: The presence of a centripetal force keeps the object moving in a circular path.

q: The centrifugal force is not a real force. (2025)
e: Centrifugal force is an apparent force resulting from an accelerating frame of reference.

q: An electron orbiting the nucleus is supported by the centrifugal force. (2025)
e: An electron orbiting the nucleus is held in place by the electrostatic force of attraction, which acts as the centripetal force.

q: Centrifugal force in a circular motion is not a real force. (2025)
e: Centrifugal force is a pseudo or fictitious force.

q: A satellite orbiting a planet is supported by the centrifugal force. (2025)
e: A satellite orbiting a planet is held in orbit by the gravitational force acting as the centripetal force.

q: Centripetal and centrifugal forces are equal. (2026)
e: Centripetal and centrifugal forces act in different frames of reference and do not form an action-reaction pair.
